title: Peace of Westphalia
summary: The Peace of Westphalia was concluded on 24 October 1648. It comprised the peace treaties of Osnabrück, between the Holy Roman Empire and Sweden, and of Münster, between the Empire and France, which formally ended the Thirty Years War. The Library of Congress describes it as an important benchmark for the development of international law and a sovereignty-based international system.

uncertainty.note: Signed on 24 October 1648 at Münster and Osnabrück.

where.historical_name: Münster, Prince-Bishopric of Münster, Holy Roman Empire

importance.justification: The Peace of Westphalia established foundational principles of sovereign statehood and multilateral diplomatic congresses that structured modern international law.

related.because: Religious divisions initiated by the Reformation ignited the confessional conflicts of the Thirty Years' War that the Westphalian settlement brought to an end.
